description: Have the service's own model write an OpenQASM 3 program for a task, the engine checking each attempt against what the task asks exactly as it checks a lesson's answer, and what went wrong going back to the model for another attempt, up to `rounds` repairs. The task is an exercise in the course's form (wai.quantum.exercise/1): a title and task in words, an optional starter program, and what the program must do, as an `intent` (an exact distribution, a reference program it must equal or whose state it must prepare) or `cases` that each have one, with optional constraints (gates allowed, counts, T count, smells), at most 16 cases and 8 intents in one place, its canonical form at most 64 KiB. The answer is a job whose result is the transcript (wai.quantum.write/1): the model by name, licence and the digest of its files, every byte checked, and the arithmetic it ran in, the prompt, each attempt's program and the engine's check, and whether one passed and at what level, signed (verify_quantum_receipt checks it with the job's request). Decoding is greedy, so the same task gives the same transcript in the same arithmetic (architecture, operating system, maths library, matmul kernel). Writes take minutes and run one at a time; a client holds one queued or running write. Call it as a task, or it waits 50 s and answers with status running and an id for get_quantum_job. A service without a model refuses it (J080); quantum_service_info says under `write` whether this one has one. Each call is a new write unless it gives idempotency_key.

idempotency_key.description: A key of your making that names this run, so that a call sent again is not a second job: the same key with the same arguments answers with the job it names, for as long as the job is kept, rather than running another; the same key with other arguments is refused (J034). Make it unguessable (a UUID). A job the service interrupted is run again under its key. Without a key, every call is a new job.

max_new.description: The most tokens one reply may take, its thinking included.

rounds.description: Repairs after the first attempt, each with the engine's account of the last (J082 outside 0 to 4).

task.description: The exercise: {"title", "task", "starter", "intent" or "cases", "constraints", "job"}, as the course's exercises (wai.quantum.exercise/1); title and task may be plain strings. It must give an intent, or cases that each have one (J081).

name: write_circuit

anyOf.description: A write's job (POST /v1/write, write_circuit): queued; running, with the attempts checked so far; done, its result the transcript, sealed, with its timing beside it; or failed, cancelled or interrupted, saying why.

digests.description: The BLAKE3 digests the store keeps the write's objects under: its request, its result and its receipt.

memory_bytes.description: What it holds of the jobs' memory budget: none, since the writer's memory is its own, held to its own cap.

work.description: The most tokens its replies may take.

interruptions.description: Each time the service stopped while the write ran, in milliseconds since 1970; it is run again, once, from its stored request, and gives the same transcript.

peak_rss_bytes.description: The most memory the writer process held while it wrote, its model's mapped pages among it.

progress.description: While it runs: how many attempts the engine has checked, and the latest.

latest.description: One attempt of a write: the program the model's reply gave, its digest, and the engine's check of it against the task (wai.quantum.course-check/1, its lesson null), whose what_went_wrong went back to the model.

answered.description: Whether the reply gave a program: false for one that ended inside its thinking, of which the engine had nothing to check.

check.description: The engine's check of the program against the task (wai.quantum.course-check/1, its lesson null), whose what_went_wrong went back to the model; null when the reply gave no program.

level.description: The level the engine checked the program to; null where there is none.

thinking_closed.description: Whether the reply reached the thinking cap still thinking, and had its thinking closed for it.

thinking_tokens.description: The reply's tokens that were thinking, counted on the tokens it gave: up to and including the one that ended its thinking, all of a reply whose thinking did not end.

request.description: What a write asks: its task, and how many repairs and tokens a reply may take; kept as its canonical text (RFC 8785), which its receipt binds.

max_new.description: The most tokens one reply may take, its thinking included (default 3000).

task.description: The task: an exercise in the course's form (wai.quantum.exercise/1), with an intent, or cases that each have one.

result.description: A write's result: its transcript (wai.quantum.write/1), with the energy the writer spent on it and the service's receipt, which seals the rest with the write's request. The transcript names the task and its digest, the model by its name, licence and the digest of its files with how far they were checked and the arithmetic it ran in, the prompt by its version and digests, the decoding with its thinking cap, the memory each check's run was planned in, the engine, and each attempt with the engine's check; the same model, task, options and engine give the same transcript in the same arithmetic, so anyone who holds the model can write it again on a host whose architecture, operating system, maths library and matmul kernel are the model's here, and compare.

items.description: One attempt of a write: the program the model's reply gave, its digest, and the engine's check of it against the task (wai.quantum.course-check/1, its lesson null), whose what_went_wrong went back to the model.

answered.description: Whether the reply gave a program: false for one that ended inside its thinking, of which the engine had nothing to check.

check.description: The engine's check of the program against the task (wai.quantum.course-check/1, its lesson null), whose what_went_wrong went back to the model; null when the reply gave no program.

level.description: The level the engine checked the program to; null where there is none.

thinking_closed.description: Whether the reply reached the thinking cap still thinking, and had its thinking closed for it.

thinking_tokens.description: The reply's tokens that were thinking, counted on the tokens it gave: up to and including the one that ended its thinking, all of a reply whose thinking did not end.

check_memory_bytes.description: The memory each check's run was planned in: it decides which programs a check runs, and by which method, so two hosts with other limits can check alike only with the same.

think_max.description: The most tokens of a reply that may be thinking: a reply still thinking there has its thinking closed for it and answers in the tokens left.

service_kwh.description: A provider job: the provider's own figure.

attribution.description: Whose energy it is: the job's worker process, or none (the processor packages' over the job's window, every process on the host in it).

concurrent_jobs.description: Other jobs that ran on the host during the window.

counter.description: The package counter as seen: the longest it went between updates, and the smallest step it took.

declared.description: What the stated uncertainty covers, and what it does not.

energy.description: The CPU energy of the job's process as the kernel counts it, with its uncertainty and what it leaves out, or unmetered with the reason.

engine.description: The version of the engine (wai-quantum) that checked each attempt.

level.description: The level the engine checked the program to; null where there is none.

arch.description: The architecture the model ran on (Rust's target_arch).

checked.description: How far the model's files were checked against its manifest before they were loaded: their sizes, or every byte (BLAKE3). The model loads exactly the files the manifest lists either way. A scripted model has none.

digest.description: BLAKE3 over the canonical text of the model's file manifest (wai.quantum.model/1: each file's name, size and digest); for a scripted model, over its script.

libm.description: The platform's maths library (glibc's version, or macOS's release and build), whose exponentials and sines shape the logits: part of the arithmetic a replay must match.

matmul.description: The BF16 matmul kernel its projections took there, which fixes the arithmetic of every logit; greedy decoding gives the same tokens again only in the same.

os.description: The operating system it ran on, whose maths library its exponentials come from.

passed_round.description: The round whose program passed; null when none did.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

receipt.title: wai.quantum.receipt/2

task.description: The task, as the model was given it: its canonical form (RFC 8785), read back.

task_digest.description: BLAKE3 over the task's canonical text (RFC 8785).

timing.description: How long each attempt's reply and its check took, in seconds: beside the result and outside what its receipt seals, since time is the one thing running it again does not reproduce.

anyOf.description: A refusal as data: the message, every code in it (the last is the code), its outcome and meaning as the code's table gives them. A host that refuses for its own reasons gives the error alone.

outputSchema.description: A write's job (POST /v1/write, write_circuit): queued; running, with the attempts checked so far; done, its result the transcript, sealed, with its timing beside it; or failed, cancelled or interrupted, saying why.
